risks.title: Persistent Inflationary Pressures and Monetary Policy Dilemma
risks.summary: Inflation remains elevated above central bank targets, creating a dilemma for policymakers who must balance controlling prices with supporting economic growth. This stickiness could lead to prolonged periods of higher interest rates.
risks.watch_for: Core PCE price index, FOMC statements on inflation outlook, and central bank interest rate decisions.

risks.title: Geopolitical Tensions and Middle East Conflict Escalation
risks.summary: Ongoing conflicts, particularly in the Middle East, continue to disrupt energy markets and supply chains, leading to sharp increases in commodity prices and renewed inflationary pressures. Escalation could further destabilize global markets.
risks.watch_for: Developments in the Middle East conflict, Strait of Hormuz shipping volumes, and energy price volatility.
sources: World Bank (Global Economic Prospects - June 2026, June 11 2026)

risks.title: US Fiscal Deficits and Rising National Debt
risks.summary: Sustained large federal budget deficits are projected to push US national debt to historic levels, increasing debt-service costs and potentially crowding out private investment.
risks.watch_for: CBO's Budget and Economic Outlook reports, and Treasury debt issuance.
sources: Congressional Budget Office (Budget and Economic Outlook, July 2026)
KPMG (The two faces of the economy, January 12 2026)

risks.title: AI Investment Boom and Productivity Uncertainty
risks.summary: While AI investment is driving growth in certain sectors, there is uncertainty about the speed and extent to which these investments will translate into broad-based productivity gains, potentially leading to overvaluation concerns.
risks.watch_for: Corporate earnings reports in the tech sector, productivity growth data, and AI adoption rates.
sources: JPMorgan Private Bank (2026 Mid-Year Outlook: Promise and Pressure, June 17 2026)
World Bank (Global Economic Prospects - June 2026, June 11 2026)
Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch, March 13 2026)

risks.title: Labor Market Weakness and Affordability Concerns
risks.summary: Despite overall resilience, some sectors show signs of labor market weakness, and persistent affordability challenges for consumers, particularly concerning housing and healthcare, could dampen spending.
risks.watch_for: Monthly jobs reports (payrolls, unemployment rate), consumer confidence surveys, and housing market data.
sources: Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch, March 13 2026)
KPMG (The two faces of the economy, January 12 2026)

risks.title: Trade Policy Uncertainty and Tariff Impacts
risks.summary: Shifting trade policies and the imposition of new tariffs create uncertainty for businesses and can disrupt supply chains, impacting both imports and exports and potentially leading to larger trade deficits.
risks.watch_for: Announcements of new tariffs, trade balance data, and outcomes of trade agreement reviews.
sources: Congressional Budget Office (Updated Budgetary Projections of Tariffs, August 20 2026)

risks.title: Financial Market Volatility and Interest Rate Risk
risks.summary: Elevated interest rates and ongoing geopolitical uncertainty contribute to financial market volatility. Markets are sensitive to shifts in monetary policy expectations and potential repricing of risk.
risks.watch_for: Treasury yields (2-year and 10-year), Federal Reserve interest rate decisions, and market sentiment indicators.

risks.title: Global Growth Divergence and Emerging Market Vulnerabilities
risks.summary: While some economies show resilience, global growth is uneven, with emerging market and developing economies facing particular headwinds due to commodity price shocks, fiscal pressures, and slower income convergence.
risks.watch_for: IMF's World Economic Outlook, World Bank's Global Economic Prospects, and growth data from key emerging markets.
sources: World Bank (Global Economic Prospects - June 2026, June 11 2026)
World Bank (Global Economic Prospects -- June 2026, June 11 2026)

consensus_note: There is a broad consensus among institutions that persistent inflation, geopolitical tensions (particularly the Middle East conflict), and fiscal sustainability are key risks. While AI is seen as a growth driver, its productivity impact remains uncertain. Outlooks diverge on the precise path of inflation and the timing of monetary policy easing, with some expecting rates to remain higher for longer due to sticky inflation.
